view.stem:
求与两条射线边都相切的正半径圆周的圆心集合。两边的公共端点为 $O$，接触点允许是 $O$。分别讨论：
1）两边不共线；
2）两边是相反射线；
3）两边重合。
第1种情况中的“小扇形”指两射线之间小于 $180^\circ$ 的扇形，不受所命名角的内部区域影响。第3种情况中，$L$ 是公共支撑直线，$S$ 是以过 $O$ 的垂线为边界、包含射线前向的闭半平面。哪组集合完整对应这三种情况？

options.text:
1）两条支撑直线的两条完整角平分线，去掉 $O$；
2）过 $O$ 的公共支撑直线的垂线，去掉 $O$；
3）$S\setminus L$。

1）小扇形的角平分射线，去掉 $O$；
2）过 $O$ 的公共支撑直线的垂线，去掉 $O$；
3）$S\setminus L$。

1）小扇形的角平分射线，去掉 $O$；
2）空集；
3）$S\setminus L$。

1）小扇形的角平分射线，去掉 $O$；
2）过 $O$ 的公共支撑直线的垂线，去掉 $O$；
3）$S$ 的内部去掉 $L$。

intent.task: Determine the complete geometric shape of the center locus in noncollinear, opposite-ray and coincident-ray configurations, including vertex-contact boundaries.
intent.source_solution: Tangency forces equal positive perpendicular distances to the supporting lines and contacts on the actual rays. For noncollinear rays the supporting-line locus consists of two whole bisectors, but testing the two projections retains only the smaller-sector bisector ray without O. This does not depend on whether a named angle is reflex. Opposite rays have a common line and their only common ray point is O, so their simultaneous contact must be O; all nonzero normal offsets at O are centers. Coincident rays impose one line tangency whose foot is on the forward closed ray. Thus the centers are exactly the forward closed half-plane bounded by the normal at O, with the supporting line removed. Nonzero normal offsets remain valid because contact at O is allowed.
intent.unit_reason: One complete three-branch geometric classification requires deriving ray, punctured-line and half-plane loci, rather than recognizing 368A's already supplied equal-distance predicate. The straight and coincident boundaries distinguish genuinely different solution families without restricting the source to acute or convex angles.
limitations: Selection of the complete classification does not demonstrate independently drawing or writing the locus proof.
The three explicitly stated configurations are conditional classifications, not a claim about the textbook's unstated angle-domain convention.

rationales.derivation: Solve only the two supporting-line equal-distance equations and keep both full bisectors. For the positive coordinate-axis rays this admits C=(-1,-1), whose contact feet are (-1,0) and (0,-1), outside both rays. Its other two branch descriptions are correct but do not rescue the whole classification.
rationales.misconception: Using the full supporting-line angle-bisector locus without selecting the admissible ray branch.

rationales.derivation: For distinct noncollinear rays only the smaller-sector open bisector has two forward feet. Opposite rays require the same contact at O and hence every nonzero normal offset. For coincident rays the center's projection must be on the closed forward ray, equivalent to membership in S, and positive distance removes L. These descriptions are necessary and sufficient in all three explicitly stated configurations.

Apply the impossibility of a nonzero radius being perpendicular to two distinct supporting lines to opposite rays, ignoring that their supports coincide. In coordinates the two rays form the x-axis; C=(0,1), r=1 contacts each at O, disproving the empty-set branch.
rationales.misconception: Carrying a distinct-line nonexistence argument into the coincident-support straight-angle case.

rationales.derivation: Replace forward-ray membership t>=0 by t>0 and discard the closed half-plane boundary. For both rays the positive x-axis, C=(0,1), r=1 has valid contact O but lies on the boundary of S, so this classification omits valid centers.
rationales.misconception: Treating a ray as excluding its endpoint and losing valid vertex-contact circles.
